analysis:
Reviewed the docs/developer/build.md additions (CI runner routing note for push runs; new CI Caching section, lines ~269-273 and 295-377) and the test-only edits in scripts/test-ci-component-paths.py (lines 272, 281, 286, 288). Neither touches provider runtime code, the coordinator-provider WebSocket (TB-002), App Attest authorization (TB-011), keys, attestation or inference paths, so no asset or threat-model entry (A-001..A-019, T-0xx) is affected at runtime.

CI-relevant observations: the doc states that only pushes to master/dev save caches, PR caches are not saved, checkouts use persist-credentials:false, and PR caches restore the base branch's entries. This is a hardening posture against cache poisoning from PRs, and the doc is consistent with it. The test edits relax the 'no continue-on-error' assertions via workflow.without_cached_checkout(...), a helper defined in scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py that is not supplied. It presumably exempts the intentional continue-on-error on the cached-checkout fallback step. I could not verify that the helper strips only that one step and not other continue-on-error uses. The assertNotIn on the 'if:' line change to a multiline regex (^    if:) is a tightening of correctness, since the raw substring would now match step-level ifs from the new checkout steps.

Remaining integration questions for a later pass: (1) the actual ci.yml and provider-ci-build action.yml (not in this batch) should be checked to confirm that save-caches is gated to push on master/dev and that cache keys exclude PR-controlled data, as the doc claims; (2) without_cached_checkout should be confirmed narrow. These are CI-supply-chain concerns outside the canonical provider threat model's listed assets, and no concrete regression is evidenced in the supplied lines.
